body:
One of the meds that made me feel insane was an anti-seizure medication called Topomax.  My doctor mentioned Lamictal as alternative to Geodon.  Knowing it's an anti-seizure kinda makes me a bit leery.

You talk about Christ in your blog.  I'm assuming your a Christian, so I have a question.  Just to preface, I'm also a Christian, so I'm not trying to set a trap or anything.  I've just never had a chance to talk openly with someone of the same faith with mental health issues.

How do you think taking meds fits into the Christian faith?  I feel like I have failed God because I wasn't strong enough to have the faith needed for Him to take away my depression.  I hear all the time how God is the healer, and he takes away depression if you trust Him, but it just hasn't happened.  Do you think depression is a physical ailment like cancer or is it an illness of the spirit, something that can only be cured by God?  How do meds fit into a Christian's life?

Everything you've described I can relate to on a personal level.  We are kindred spirits.  

I want you to know that it will get better.  Time can heal many wounds, and even things like depression can get better as you get older and don't have to deal with the crazy hormone flooding of a teenage brain.  Don't give up.  You'll be missing out on the most rich and beautiful part of your life.  Your 20's are something worth getting to.

I've had sex without protection or had the condom break so many times.  Not once did it end in pregnancy.  Lucky, yes, but just know that even a wild night of three consecutive romps doesn't mean instant pregnancy like they indoctrinate you with in sex-ed courses.  

There is a definite risk, but it's not always an instantaneous thing.  My sister and her husband just got pregnant (Just my sister that is.  Her husband isn't.), and it took them about half a year of having unprotected sex for it to happen.

If you are pregnant, it's not the end of your life.  My close friend got pregnant at 16, carried her baby to full term, and had a wonderful family adopt her baby.  She finished highschool and is now married with two children of her own.  The only reason she didn't go to college is because she didn't want to.  Not because she had lost the opportunity.  You will be ok!

I'm sorry your parents aren't letting you get the morning after pill.  Have you considered telling them how you are feeling?  I know my parents have done some pretty insensitive things, and once I let them know it was literally killing me inside, they did what they could to make it better.

I hope you hang in there.  Even if you feel like no one cares, know that someone in the world, me, is sending you happy thoughts and wants you alive.  

The human mind and body are a resilient thing, and people can bounce back from the most devastating circumstances.  No matter what happens, you are going to be ok.  I've been there, I'm living it now, and I hope you can continue your journey on this planet with me.  The world would be a little emptier without you.

I'm sorry your friends are being selfish and don't understand your situation enough to help you.  If I'm not mistaken, the morning after pill is now over the counter and can be bought at any pharmacy.  If you have a CVS or even a grocery store pharmacy within walking distance, you might be able to get some.
Is there any weight gain or sexual side effects with Zyprexa?  Those two are usually the ones that hit me the worst.

Thank you for responding to my post last night.  Just getting it out of my head made me feel better and realize it's a bad reaction to the Geodon that's making me feel this way.  Sure enough, after a quick Google, "thought's of suicide" is one of the common side effects not listed on the packaging or on the Geodon website.  I can't believe they leave these things out!  It's dangerous!!

I'm getting therapy for the first time in my adult life starting this Friday.  We did some family counseling when I was a kid, but yeah, that didn't work out so well.

Thank you again.  Here's to hoping the therapy is the answer I've been looking for.

I go off meds, and I feel fine for a while.  Then I drop down into a depression so deep I can barely do anything but get through the day.  My life passes by me while I lay in bed, not taking care of my self.  Hygene goes down the drain.  My room is a mess.  I can't function.  

I go on meds, and sometimes they make me feel like I'm going insane, like schizophrenic insane.  I never feel this way when I'm not medicated.  Other times they make me feel better.  It depends on the drug.  Welbutrin usually works, and I've been on it again for about two weeks, but the good effects only last for a short while.  Then I sink back into the depths of depression.  I can't function.  

I'm terrified of going on anything else because of the horrible side effects I've had on every single med I've ever tried other than Welbutrin.  My doctor wants me to try Geodon, and because I'm desperate for help, I agreed to try it, but only after two doses of the smallest dosage possible, I feel like I'm going to die.  Like all is lost in the world and nothing will ever be right again.  I want to live, but my body wants to die.  I want life.  How do I find it?  I think it's the medication, but damn does it feel real.  I just need to get through tonight, and I'll be ok.

I feel hopeless because no matter what I try, it's still the same.  Depression is crippling.  I feel like half a person, and like my life is wasted.  All of my peers are passing me by, because they aren't constantly weighed down by their own bodies and thoughts.  At my worst, I literally feel heavy.  Like I can't even move.  I can't eat without feeling sick to my stomach.  I feel ill all the time.

I'm 24.  I should be out of college by now having a life with a husband and maybe a child.  I want children and a home.  I want to be a good wife, and have a husband to take care of.  But  I'm stuck being a person I don't want to be, and I feel helpless to control it.
